Variants.Content: Jorah Mormont is the son of Jeor Mormont and once inherited the barren Bear Island. A dazzling jousting victory and a marriage far beyond the financial resources of Bear Island made him desperately pursue a life he could not support; when debts loomed, he sold poachers to slave traders, violated the laws of the North, and fled to Essos before Ned Stark came to judge. Exile made him a hedge knight, a guide, and a man seeking his place in a strange court. He later becomes close to Daenerys Targaryen, and his loyalty to her, his love for her, and his desire to be forgiven are all intertwined with his concealment. Jorah carries the weight of Bear Island, his father, and his lost honor, but these choices belong only to him and do not mean that the Mormont family has left the North.

It's hard for Northerners to forget Jorah's sin of selling poachers. The poverty of Bear Island can explain his plight, but love and debt cannot change what the slave trade violated. Some people still remember his bravery, while others only remember that he escaped Ned's sword; both memories left a scar on the Black Bear family name.

The people of Essos looked at Jorah more like an exiled knight familiar with many languages, roads, and employers. He understands Westeros and how to survive without belonging. Such guides are useful, but they always make people wonder how much a person who desperately wants to be needed by someone will hide the truth about not wanting to lose the other person.

If slaves and freedmen knew that Jorah had sold people into slavery, it would be difficult to see him only as a loyal knight at the Queen's side. A person can regret and save others, but he still has to bear the burden of what he has done. For them, the real atonement is not to say who they love, but to face the people they once regarded as goods.
